title: Tanzanian Chicken Curry
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Kuku — chicken simmered in a rich tomato-coconut curry sauce fragrant with Tanzanian spices, fresh coriander, and green chilli. The everyday chicken curry of Tanzania — warming, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.
longDesc: Tanzanian chicken curry is distinct from Indian curry — it is built on a tomato base rather than yogurt, uses coconut milk for richness, and the spicing is warmer than it is hot. It is the chicken dish that appears at every Tanzanian family meal, mama lishe stall, and celebration table.
steps: Brown chicken pieces in oil. Remove.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, and chillies. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until thick.
Simmer covered for 30—35 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
chefTips: Bone-in chicken gives the best flavour.
Add coconut milk after the tomato base is well reduced — prevents splitting.
cookingScience: Coconut milk contains proteins that stabilise at lower temperatures but break down above 82°C — never letting it reach a hard boil keeps the sauce smooth and emulsified.
culturalNote: Chicken curry is Tanzania's most universally eaten meat dish — chicken is more affordable than goat or beef, and this fragrant curry makes it magnificent.
